hints.title: Salary Bracket Definitions
hints.text: Categorize accounts into three fixed buckets: Low Salary (income < 20000), Average Salary (income between 20000 and 50000 inclusive), and High Salary (income > 50000).

hints.title: Ensuring Complete Category Coverage
hints.text: Every category must appear in the final output even if zero accounts fall into that salary band.

hints.title: Union of Fixed Bands
hints.text: Compute the count for each category individually using three select statements joined together with union all.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    'Low Salary' AS category,
    COUNT(account_id) AS accounts_count
FROM Accounts
WHERE income < 20000
UNION ALL
SELECT
    'Average Salary' AS category,
    COUNT(account_id) AS accounts_count
FROM Accounts
WHERE income >= 20000 AND income <= 50000
UNION ALL
SELECT
    'High Salary' AS category,
    COUNT(account_id) AS accounts_count
FROM Accounts
WHERE income > 50000;
```

complexity.time: O(N) where N is number of accounts
complexity.space: O(1) output records fixed at 3 rows
variables: N: number of accounts in Accounts table
complexity.notes: Three category counts combined via UNION ALL.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: A simple group by drops categories with zero matching accounts.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Scanning the table 3 times or aggregating conditional sums keeps the result size constant.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that empty categories must not be omitted from the output.
